answer.generated: Concurrent transactions may modify the same data resource simultaneously, leading to conflicts that require concurrency control mechanisms such as locks. In file-processing systems, locks are used to manage access to shared files, ensuring that only one transaction at a time can update a specific record. Similarly, in database systems, locks are applied to data items to prevent race conditions during concurrent updates. Without proper lock management, conflicting transactions could corrupt data integrity. Thus, locks are a core component of concurrency control, enabling safe multitransaction processing in both file-processing and database environments.
